draft.title: Stars, galaxies and the universe
card: A star is a huge ball of hot gas that gives off its own light. The Sun is a star.
Stars are grouped in galaxies, held together by gravity. Our galaxy is the Milky Way, and it holds hundreds of billions of stars.
The universe is everything that exists: all galaxies, stars, planets, gas and space. It holds billions of galaxies.
A light-year is a distance, not a time. It is how far light travels in one year, which is about 9.5 trillion kilometres.
draft.remember: Stars make up galaxies, galaxies make up the universe, and light-years measure the huge gaps.

opts: The distance light travels in one year
The time light takes to leave a star
The age of a star in years
The brightness of a star over one year
a.why: A light-year is a distance: how far light travels in a year. It is easy to think it is a time because it has the word year in it, but it is used for the huge distances between stars and galaxies.
a.clue: Think about what light does during that year.

b.q: Which list puts these in order from smallest to largest?
opts: Star, galaxy, universe
Galaxy, star, universe
Star, universe, galaxy
Universe, galaxy, star
b.why: Stars are grouped into galaxies, and the universe holds billions of galaxies. So a star is the smallest and the universe is the largest. Galaxy is not smaller than a star, because a galaxy is made of stars.
b.clue: Which one is made up of the one before it?

problems.detail: "Stars make up galaxies, galaxies make up the universe" is neater than the card. The card defines the universe as everything, including planets, gas and space, not just galaxies. Galaxies also contain gas and dust as well as stars. Suggest "Stars are grouped in galaxies, and the universe holds billions of galaxies".
